title: The average that never settles
question: The average that never settles
hook: You have averaged a thousand data points — and the very next point moves your average as if you had barely started.
core_idea: The Central Limit Theorem requires finite variance; in heavy-tailed (Cauchy-like) worlds the running mean never converges, so average-loss evaluation measures a quantity that does not exist.
visual_object: two running-mean traces racing side by side — Gaussian settling, Cauchy lurching
prerequisites: sample mean, passing familiarity with the bell curve
exclusions: no stable-distribution theory, no power-law taxonomy, no tail-index estimation
